kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the printed naming table — 4 patterns (the chimeric -ximab infusion-reaction stem, the -tinib intracellular-tyrosine-kinase stem, the -leukin interleukin-2 agonist/analog stem, the -umab fully-human formulary question), 4 traps (-ximab/-zumab/-umab source ladder, -tinib vs -zomib infix machines, -leukin vs -kinra directions, -mab vs -ib target addresses), 3 pivots (the source-infix router, the stem/format router, the cytokine-direction router), and 8 recall cards covering all 11 printed rows.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the ending→category→example associations only; the attack structure, the distractor designs, and the reverse-direction question shapes are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The stem→infix→direction grammar and the four-move decode protocol (READ THE STEM -mab/-ib/-kin → IF -mab READ THE SOURCE INFIX -xi-/-zu-/-u- → IF -ib/-kin READ THE TARGET INFIX OR DIRECTION → RECALL THE PRINTED EXAMPLE, THEN GENERALIZE), including the format-follows-the-target rule (cell-surface receptor → antibody; intracellular molecule → small molecule; interleukin receptor → recombinant modulator) — the claim that this three-row -mab grammar decodes every monoclonal on the exam.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the three source infixes and their categories as table rows but never states the grammar (read the name right-to-left), the delivery logic, or the protocol; the synthesis is KYP's.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + mechanisms[0] + blocks[2] the list block + blocks[3] the steps block + the registry visual's Zone A ladder, Zone B panel, and Zone D protocol strip

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP mnemonics (XI MIXES, ZU GRAFTS, U IS HUMAN / MAB OUTSIDE, IB INSIDE, KIN IN-BETWEEN / SIX MACHINES, ONE SUFFIX / LEUKIN LIFTS, KINRA KNOCKS). No mnemonic prints in the page's margins; First Aid's own red mnemonic letters INSIDE the CATEGORY cells (Chi-meric, Humanized, Human, Cyclin-, COX-2, Poly, BRAF, Tyrosine kinase, Proteasome, Interleukin-2, interleukin receptor antagonist) are carried ATTRIBUTED inside the verbatim table, the memory callout, and the visual, and are NOT counted among the four KYP codes.
kypExtensions.rationale: No margin mnemonic prints anywhere on pdf 276 (pdfimages + VLM census, staging-ph28/vlm-census.txt); the four ALL-CAPS codes are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: mnemonics + blocks[6] the memory callout + the visual's footer attribution text

kypExtensions.summary: The rituximab first-infusion-reaction miniCase — which ending marks the monoclonal class — with the correct answer routing the structural description (murine variable regions + human constant regions = the printed 'Chimeric human-mouse monoclonal antibody' category verbatim) to -ximab, and distractors climbing the wrong rung (-zumab humanized, -umab human) or leaving the antibody family entirely (-kinra, the interleukin receptor antagonist).
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the pairing as one table row and never dissects it against the ladder's other rungs as distractors; the vignette, the four options, and the reasoning are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The KYP-context generalizations, every one flagged as such: the -mab grammar applied to monoclonals the page never prints (infliximab -xi- chimeric, trastuzumab -zu- humanized, adalimumab -u- human), the immunogenicity shadow of the humanization ladder (chimeric > humanized > human), the specific receptor context for the -kin rows (aldesleukin at the IL-2 receptor driving T-cell expansion; anakinra as the recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist), and the -ib indication families — the immunology bridge to the cytokine physiology.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source is a naming table with category words only; every mechanism, receptor, indication, and immunogenicity statement beyond the printed categories is KYP context, explicitly marked in the note and never presented as printed text.
kypExtensions.location: blocks[2] the list block + mechanisms[1] cytokine-mimic-map + blocks[4] the compare block + blocks[5] the exam callout + mnemonics' clinical fields
